newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks rise during week over new reforms.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks rise during week over new reforms.

text.p: Trading on Jordan's exchange was buoyed during the week as investors reacted favourably to a long-awaited package of free-market reforms in the wake of recent bread riots, dealers said.

The Amman Financial Market official 60-share index rose 2.14 percent at the end of weekly trading on Wednesday to 142.54 points from 139.54 points the previous trading week, the exchange's weekly report released on Friday showed.
It was the highest rise since the end of June, when minimal institutional support and lack of cash liquidity sent the index below 140 points, sliding to levels not reached since 1993.

Investor sentiment, dampened after recent unrest fueled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms, was boosted after Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti pledged to encourage private sector investment, dealers said.
The market reacted favourably to a new companies law that would cancel a 15 percent tax levied on companies' capital increases.
Heavy demand on blue-chip Arab Bank -- a major component of the official 60-share index -- helped further buttress prices during the week, with a high 7.500 dinar rise to 229 dinars.

Investors say the 44 million dinar capitalised Arab Bank, the kingdom's leading bank, is a main beneficiary of the new draft companies law. Its management has promised to distribute a bonus share to its shareholders once the tax is cancelled.
The value of shares traded in the five-day period -- in both the official and primary market -- rose 34.6 percent to 3.5 million dinars from 2.6 million dinars the previous week.
Daily average trading rose to nearly 0.7 million dinars from 0.5 million dinars the previous week.

Industrials shares, the most active sector, accounted for 50.6 percent of weekly value on a volume of 1.79 million dinars, followed by 35.6 percent for banks on a volume of 1.26 million dinars, and 13.5 percent for services on a volume of 0.48 million dinars and 0.3 percent for insurance.

In industrials, key industrials continue to buttress the sector: Jordan Cement Factories rose 100 fils during the week to 3.370 dinars and Jordan Petroleum Refinery Company was unchanged at 9.290 dinars. Livestock and Poultry rose 60 fils to 550 fils.
In services, Jordan Electric Power was unchanged during the week to 1.530 dinars. National Securities Portfolio rose 30 fils to 1.190 dinars.
In the week, 2,645 orders were executed for 2.9 million shares. Thirty five shares were higher, 34 lower and 21 unchanged.
